definitions.explanation: A person who behaves rudely toward someone, especially toward a superior. Best known as an angry exclamation in period dramas.

examples.japanese: 「{無礼者|ぶれいもの}！」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{殿様|とのさま}→殿様：10455_tonosama⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{叫|さけ}んだ→叫ぶ：02108_sakebu⟧。
⟦あんな→あんな：01574_anna⟧{無礼者|ぶれいもの}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{付|つ}き{合|あ}いたくない→付き合う：02291_tsukiau⟧。
examples.english: I don't want anything to do with such an insolent fellow.

examples.japanese: ⟦{時代劇|じだいげき}→時代劇：12968_jidaigeki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{身分|みぶん}→身分：00278_mibun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧「{無礼者|ぶれいもの}」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{怒鳴|どな}る→怒鳴る：05340_donaru⟧⟦{場面|ばめん}→場面：03702_bamen⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{出|で}てくる→出てくる：29121_detekuru⟧。
examples.english: Period dramas often have scenes where a person of high rank shouts "Insolent wretch!"

notes:
USAGE:
Old-fashioned. Today it is mostly heard in period dramas, shouted by a lord or samurai at someone beneath them. In modern speech, people say ⟦{失礼|しつれい}→失礼：01247_shitsurei⟧な⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ or ⟦{無礼|ぶれい}→無礼：15041_burei⟧な⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{無礼|ぶれい}→無礼：15041_burei⟧: rudeness, insolence
- ⟦{失礼|しつれい}→失礼：01247_shitsurei⟧: rude, impolite (the everyday word)
